phaseBreakdown.note: Phase counts cover items NOT YET DONE (OPEN + WIP + BUILT + DECISION). FIXED and CLEARED items are assigned to NO phase, which is why the phase totals do not approach the release total. BUILT means implemented and awaiting certification - it is NOT outstanding work.

legend.FIXED: Implemented and verified. Tracker verdict DONE or MET.
legend.BUILT: Implemented, not yet certified by a full release run. Tracker verdict PARTIAL, BUILT or IN PROGRESS — the code landed, the suite that would prove it has not run.
legend.OPEN: Confirmed, not started. Tracker verdict TODO, or a defect nobody marked closed.
legend.DECISION: Blocked on an owner decision or an owner action. Tracker verdict BLOCKED or DEFERRED, or a TODO the tracker marks as the owner's.
legend.CLEARED: Not applicable — the premise was false, or the item is counted against another row. Tracker verdict N/A.
legend.ON HOLD: Parked, and NOT actionable by us. Blocked on something the owner has declined or cannot do yet, such as a paid plan tier or an external dependency. Tracker verdict HELD, ON HOLD or PARKED. Distinct from DECISION, which is waiting on an owner ANSWER we have asked for.

directives.text: No Vercel preview deployments. Every non-main deployment must land CANCELED — CANCELED is free, BUILDING/READY/ERROR is billed.
A push is the only Actions-consuming action a push approval covers. Reruns, workflow_dispatch, a second push or a non-draft PR are each a fresh ask.
A commit hash AND a verification that ran AND a user-invocable outcome. Two of three is not done.
A gate that cannot fail is not a gate. Prove it fails before trusting that it passed, and take exit codes from UNPIPED commands.
A record of a thing is not the thing. Measure the artefact, not the comment, filename or tracker row describing it.
This board is DERIVED from the release tracker and defect register. Where they disagree with it, THEY WIN.

MANDATORY for every release, every session: start by reading this board. Be able to state total raised, how many are done, and of the rest how many are not started / written-awaiting-certification / awaiting an owner decision — INCLUDING which population each number belongs to. The headline counts and the per-phase counts measure different things; subtracting one from the other gives a wrong answer.

At release close every item goes to exactly ONE place: still pending (not started, built, or awaiting a decision) HANDS OVER to the next release with its evidence; done and cleared are SAVED AS RELEASE DELIVERY. The board then re-points at the new release. Nothing is dropped at a boundary. See docs/STATUS-BOARD-CHARTER.md.

If a status cannot express the truth, ADD THE STATE — never pick the nearest wrong one. Twice this release a status was falsified by a missing word: built-but-not-shipped read as FIXED, and withdrawn read as OPEN forever. A phantom OPEN is as damaging as a phantom FIXED.
crowagent-platform-web + crowagent-portal get FOUR Vercel production deploys for the whole release — ONE at each phase boundary. Nothing mid-phase, for any reason, including a docs-only commit.
crowagent-website is SEPARATE. It does not count against that budget and ships as and when ready.
Railway, staging AND production: deploy whenever needed. No approval, no waiting.
Supabase, staging AND production: apply whenever needed. No approval, no waiting. Via MCP apply_migration, never db push.
There is no Phase 5. Phase 2 is CLOSED. Every remaining item is Phase 3 or Phase 4.
Never report deploy or phase state from a repository document or git log. Read the live surface — Vercel, Stripe, Supabase, Railway.

issues.title: [SEV:P1][LANE:PORTAL] the 12 month MRR chart repeats a single value across twelve columns
issues.note: VERIFIED MYSELF on production: portal_mrr_snapshots holds exactly ONE row, and staging holds zero. The route serves real snapshots only when at least twelve months are covered, so it ALWAYS takes the flat back fill. The result is a chart whose SHAPE asserts twelve months of stable revenue, drawn from one measurement. There is a caption, in the smallest type in the legend row. This is the "measure the thing, not the record of it" defect rendered as a graph, and a shape is a stronger claim than a sentence, so a caption cannot carry the correction. Fix: refuse to draw the series until enough snapshots exist, and say how many months are actually covered, rather than drawing a flat line and explaining it in small print. Related: portal-mrr-snapshot is one of the seven portal crons, so the corpus does grow, one row a day, and the chart becomes honest on its own once twelve months exist.

issues.title: [SEV:P0][LANE:PORTAL] publishing a regulation update reports success for an email fan out that is structurally impossible
issues.note: VERIFIED MYSELF, and it is worse than the report said. apps/portal/src/app/api/regulation-updates/route.ts:93 posts to ${railwayUrl}/api/v1/core/regulatory-update-email. THE CORE ROUTERS WERE DELETED: api/app/main.py:617 mounts only /api/v1/core/zapier under that prefix, so the target is a 404. The call sits in a try whose catch logs and then execution CONTINUES to return NextResponse.json with a published status. AND THE CATCH DOES NOT EVEN FIRE: fetch does NOT throw on a 404, it resolves with ok: false, and the response is never inspected. So the failure is invisible even in the log that was written to catch it. The operator is told the update was published and the emails queued. Nothing was queued and nothing can be. THIS IS WORSE THAN A STUB, because a stub does not assert an outcome. Fix: check res.ok, and report the fan out result separately from the publish result, because a stored update with no email is a legitimate partial outcome that the caller must be told about rather than a success.

issues.title: [SEV:P2][LANE:PRODUCT] the compliance advisor ANSWERS CORRECTLY and the user sees none of it: the reply is revealed by requestAnimationFrame with no fallback, under a "no source document was matched" caption that can essentially never be satisfied

The threshold is sized against the drain curve rather than by feel: draining a backlog of B takes ln(1 + 3.5B/220)/3.5, about 1.5 s for 10,000 characters and 2.1 s for 100,000, so a reveal still incomplete at 3 s is STOPPED rather than merely slow. issues.title: [SEV:P1][LANE:SECURITY] a caller supplied Salesforce host receives the organisation's OAuth credentials
issues.note: FOUND 2026-09-08 while promoting the SSRF guard, REPORTED RATHER THAN FIXED because the router sits outside that work's file ownership. It is the SAME defect as the PostHog client that row closed, in Python, and it is LIVE. api/app/routers/crm.py ConnectRequest.instance_url accepts a URL from the caller with no egress validation, and the stored value reaches app/services/crm_salesforce.py:136, which POSTs the organisation's Salesforce credentials to f'{self._instance_url}/services/oauth2/token'.
